title: Weighted kernel multiplexer and clock-budget manager for mixed-SKU MIG fleets
creator: Priya Raman
description: Implement a runtime component that scores and multiplexes kernel candidates per request across mixed-SKU (H100/L40S/A10) MIG partitions and enforces a per-slice clock budget manager. The goal is to reduce 95th-percentile prefill/decode latency regressions under heterogeneous fleets while keeping thermal headroom and unit-cost targets. This ticket covers the algorithm, integration with telemetry hints, a lightweight policy engine, and the first production rollout behind a canary toggle.
acceptance_criteria: 95th-percentile prefill latency reduced by >=12% on representative mixed-MIG workloads compared to baseline without multiplexer
No more than 3% regression in median decode latency for single-SKU H100 runs after enabling clock budget enforcement
Automated fallback: if kernel candidate selection fails or degrades SLOs, the system falls back to default kernel schedule within 500ms
End-to-end traceable decision logs emitted to console traces for every routed request (sampling at 1%)
Canary rollout completed to 10% of Dedicated capacity with monitoring dashboards and automatic rollback on cost/latency regression thresholds
technical_notes: Score = weighted sum(kernel_score, runtime_estimate, thermal_headroom, kv_cache_hit_prob) where weights are config-driven and hot-reloadable
Kernel candidates include: native fast-attn kernels (fp16/fp32), quantized-fallback kernels, and sparse-aware kernels when model supports sparsity hints
Clock Budget Manager exposes per-MIG-slice budgets (GHz*s window) with soft/cold policies: soft=prefer cheaper kernel, cold=throttle clocks and prefer fallback kernels
Telemetry hooks: use hw_telemetry and token_density probes from existing pipeline (see ENG-271900) to adapt weights per minute
Prefer stateless decision path for the fast path (<100us decision latency) with an async re-ranker for long-running requests to refine kernel chaining
Introduce a metrics set: kernel_choice, kernel_latency_est, chosen_clock_turbine, thermal_headroom_post_choice, decision_latency_ms
progress_updates: 2025-11-06: Spike completed - implemented scoring prototype in runtime local branch; basic weighted selector picks between native-attn and quant-fallback based on simple heuristics
2025-11-09: Microbenchmarks on H100 (single-SKU) show no median regression; mixed-MIG synthetic load shows 8-10% 95th reduction with naive weights
2025-11-12: Discovered regression under bursty short-sequence workloads due to decision path CPU jitter; mitigated by caching last-choice per model+seq-len bucket
2025-11-15: Integrated per-slice clock budget REST endpoint and simulated clock caps; observed improved thermal headroom but decode median increased by 2% in worst-case — evaluating weight tuning
2025-11-18: Added trace logging format and sample traces for 1% requests; initial traces pushed to tracing cluster (trace-id example: trace:abc123).
2025-11-20: Canary plan drafted; dashboards instrumented (dashboard link below). Preparing PR for review (#2137)
review_feedback: PM (Janelle Ortiz): prioritize safe rollback triggers and clear cost telemetry to avoid unexpected spend when multiplexer routes to more expensive kernels
SRE (Marco Li): ensure the decision path doesn't allocate or block runtime worker threads; prefer lock-free structures and use bounded ring buffers for async re-ranking
Design (Ana Guerrero): request clearer UI flags in Console for per-customer toggles and visibility into kernel choices per route
Eng review (Tomas Novak): suggest a lightweight ML model later for weight tuning, but keep initial config rule-based to simplify rollout and A/B analysis
benchmark_results: Mixed-MIG synthetic (H100+L40S, 70/30 split, seq_len=256): baseline 95th prefill=190ms, candidate multiplexer=167ms (-12.1%)
Burst short sequences (seq_len=16) on A10-saturated nodes: naive multiplexer increased median decode by 2.3% before caching last-choice; after caching delta ~+0.4%
Power/thermal simulation: clock budget enforcement preserved headroom, lowering average package temperature by ~4C under sustained load
Cost estimation: estimated per-token GPU cost change within +/-1.5% for default weights; worst-case paths <+6% which will be mitigated with policy caps
next_steps: Finalize PR #2137 addressing Marco's lock-free feedback and add more unit tests for decision path
Run 48-hour canary on Dedicated cluster at 10% capacity with automatic rollback thresholds: 95th latency +12% or cost +8%
Tune default weight set using production-like workloads and add small online feedback loop to nudge weights once canary is stable
Add Console controls and per-customer override flags as requested by Design
Plan follow-up: investigate lightweight learning-based tuner (ENG spike) if rule-based weights plateau
